headline: Cloudflare injects analytics by default for free plans when switching nameservers
summary: Cloudflare integrates Real User Measurement (RUM) into free plans, enabling performance data collection and access to its Observatory tool. This feature is on by default but can be disabled.
details: Cloudflare has been observed injecting its Real User Measurement (RUM) analytics script into websites using its free plans. This occurs by default when site owners switch their nameservers to Cloudflare.

The company states that RUM provides site owners with actionable performance data they might not otherwise have. It also grants free plans access to their Observatory product, a performance-monitoring tool.

Cloudflare clarifies that RUM is on by default for free sites, a decision explained in a blog post titled "The RUM Diaries." They emphasize that the feature is easy to disable if users prefer not to have it active.
For all paid Cloudflare plans, the RUM analytics feature is opt-in only. This distinction highlights different default behaviors based on subscription tiers.

The practice of injecting scripts into response bodies, even for analytics, raises discussions about third-party intervention. Cloudflare operates as a Man-in-the-Middle (MiTM) when directing traffic through its proxies.

This scenario is typically a concern cited against ISPs for potential script injection. Cloudflare's approach, however, has generally faced fewer objections, possibly due to its perceived benefits and user control options.
